quote.text: I'm the one everybody asks what happens next

promise.text: How to plan a group trip (without being the organizer)

art.why: the carousel's topic: the moment and its guide name "trip", "group"

lines.text: Group trips go wrong when one person holds everything in their head.
Decide who books what, who is on each booking and where the answers live.

head.text: List everyone who is definitely in, and everyone who is a maybe with a date you'll stop waiting.

body.text: A maybe with no deadline holds up every booking.

head.text: List what needs booking: transport, lodging, anything with a reserved time.

body.text: For each, name one person who makes the booking.
Not who pays, who makes it.

head.text: Mark each item fixed or optional.

body.text: Flights and lodging are usually fixed.
Everything else should be optional in plain words, so nobody feels obliged to join the museum.

head.text: Write down who is on each booking.

body.text: Four on the flight, three in the car, five at the dinner.
This is the step people skip, and it's the one that stops someone discovering at the airport that they were never on a booking.

head.text: Note what each person needs once: meals, a seat, mobility, medication that changes timing.

body.text: Recorded against the person, it's there when a booking is made, not remembered afterward.

line.text: Today shows the current state of the trip in plain sentences, each tracing to something somebody recorded, so the answer is not in your head alone.
